entry.title: Tutor: nineteen fixes from an audit
entry.content:
Tutor: nineteen fixes from an audit

Answer integrity: the header shows the side the card asks, not the French
front; the tutor is told whether the card has been answered and withholds
the answer until it has; "just got this wrong" now comes from this attempt
(with what was typed), not last session's row; Add never overwrites an
existing card — it offers Replace, which changes only the back.

Quality: earlier turns keep the card they were about and the cards proposed;
card rules (arrow drills for grammar, no pronunciation cards) in the prompt
and enforced server-side; misses sent only when recent and relevant; deck
matching handles accents, elision, œ and curly apostrophes, and follow-ups.

Robustness and cost: a stream without "done" reads as cut off; max_tokens and
refusal surfaced; raw API errors kept out of the UI; the conversation is
cached (the system prompt alone is under Sonnet 5's 1,024-token minimum);
Add inserts the returned row instead of refetching the deck.

Panel: New chat, and a fresh thread when opened from another card;
card-aware suggestions; bold/italic rendered; focus stays in the box; study
keys work beside the tutor until you click into it; screen-reader
announcement; the thread survives the onboarding-to-app swap and clears on
sign-out.

Feedback panel moves into the sidebar; closing keeps the draft, sending says so

  flipping or grading it.

entry.title: The Stats page speaks seen and remembered; "mastered" is gone
entry.content:
The Stats page speaks seen and remembered; "mastered" is gone

Stages 6 and 7 of the serving strategy.

Stats:
  - Today and Right first time today replace This session and Accuracy,
    counted off each card's last_review. Exact across blocks, reloads and
    devices, because FSRS now gets one answer per card per day.
  - One three-band bar for the whole deck (about remembered / seen, not
    currently remembered / not yet seen) replaces new / learning / mastered.
  - Your progress: a row per lesson, recent classes and earlier notes.
  - Coming up: cards due on each of the next seven days, so a review-heavy
    stretch after a big day of new cards is visible before it arrives.
  - By type keeps accuracy and shows seen / about remembered. Its "none
    studied yet" now keys off cards seen, not the legacy accuracy tally.
  - Streak, Hardest cards and Reset unchanged.

Not built: the agreed finish estimates. Pace needs to know when each card
was first seen, and nothing records that; it would take a first_seen_at
column. Written up as an open item for the owner to decide.

Tidy-up: MASTERED_STABILITY_DAYS becomes SPOT_CHECK_MIN_STABILITY_DAYS,
cardStage is deleted, the counter says "spot check", and the freqOnly filter
no control ever set is removed. The admin users table keeps its legacy
"Mastered" column (card_progress score >= 3); no student sees it.

Tests: new `stats` suite, expected figures counted from its own fixture.
Full suite on this Mac: 15 of 18; layout, motion and reflow fail the same
Mac-Chrome way as on commits before this work.

entry.title: The checkpoint after each block, and the lesson's progress in its top…
entry.content:
The checkpoint after each block, and the lesson's progress in its top bar

Stages 4 and 5 of the serving strategy.

"Session complete!" and New Session are replaced by a checkpoint
(data-checkpoint): how the block went ("50 cards, 43 right first time",
counting first answers of the day in either mode), what each area moved, and
then Continue, "You're in a review phase" when the next block would hold no
new cards, or "You're all caught up" with no Continue into an empty block.
Inside a lesson it also says how many cards elsewhere are due. The block
counter hides at the checkpoint.

Continue deals the next block from the deck in memory. useUserDeck gains
patch(), and every recorded answer is applied to the local deck as well as
written; building from a refetch could return a card's pre-answer state
before the write lands, deal it again, and record a second review.

Inside a lesson the top bar reads "about 43 of 108 remembered"
(data-lesson-progress), taken when the block is dealt and at its checkpoint,
never per answer.

Found while testing the bar: a full rebuild kept the card on screen by
jumping to its position in the new shuffled block, so entering a lesson could
start at card 35 of 50, skip 34 cards and end after 16 answers. A new block
now always starts at card 1, with the card on screen moved to the front, and
its counts reset.

Tests: session works a 113-card backlog through three blocks (review-phase
message, Continue, all caught up, exactly 113 writes); lessons checks the
block starts at card 1, the bar doesn't move per answer, and reads about 50
after a block of 50.

entry.title: Blocks of 50: due cards first, new cards only once they run out
entry.content:
Blocks of 50: due cards first, new cards only once they run out

Stage 2 of the serving strategy agreed with the owner on 2026-09-12.

buildSession now deals a block of up to 50:
  1. cards missed last time, due today
  2. other due cards, most overdue first
  3. new cards, only in the room the due cards leave
  4. two spot checks, only alongside real work, never a card answered today
then shuffles it, as before.

"Due" is due any time today on the student's clock (endOfLocalDay), so the
day's work doesn't grow while they study.

This reverses the rule that reserved new-card slots ahead of due work. A
student behind on reviews gets review-only blocks until caught up; the
builder returns dueRemaining so the checkpoint can say so.

New cards come in a real order instead of at random (orderNewCards):
  - in a lesson: the lesson's teachingOrder, which puts each exercise straight
    after its rule (the card array lists every rule before any exercise)
  - otherwise: recent classes (last 14 days) newest first, then earlier notes
    by how many classes a word came up in, older class on a tie, then undated
    cards, then unseen lesson cards so a student with no notes still has
    something to learn
Tutor chat cards are dated by created_at, now loaded with the deck (checked
against the live table first: the column exists and is populated).

Tests: new browserless `serving` suite, one check per rule, under a pinned
timezone. Full suite on this Mac: 14 of 16; layout and motion fail the same
Mac-Chrome way as on commits before this one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: FSRS gets one answer per card per day: the first
entry.content:
FSRS gets one answer per card per day: the first

The retry after a miss wrote a second FSRS review minutes after the student
had been shown the answer, and so did answering a card again after Previous
card. The scheduler runs with short-term steps off, so it read each of those
as evidence about memory across days. Measured against this app's settings,
it moved the schedule the wrong way every time:

  known card, missed, right on the retry   due in 3 days -> 4, and the miss
                                           flag cleared, so it lost its place
                                           at the front of the next session
  missed, then wrong again on the retry    counted as forgotten twice,
                                           difficulty near its maximum
  new card, missed, right on the retry     due tomorrow -> 3 days

answer() now skips the scheduler write when the card's own last_review falls
on the student's local day (reviewedToday in lib/studyDay). The card is still
shown and graded on screen. Reading it off the card rather than tracking
retries in the session also covers a reload mid-session and a second device.

Tests: dates checks the day rule under a pinned timezone, including 9pm and
10pm in New York landing on different UTC days; session misses a card, answers
its retry, steps back and answers two cards again, and counts one PATCH per
card.

The context doc records the serving strategy agreed with the owner today,
with this as stage 1 of 7 and the rest marked unbuilt.

Full suite on this Mac: 12 of 15 pass. layout, motion and reflow fail
identically on HEAD without this change and on 9b95052, which passed all 15
in the container, so they are this machine's Chrome build, not the code.
